steps.do: Create the docs folder for the accessibility plan.
Create the empty plan file that will hold the timing decision.
Write a base dismiss time of 6 seconds, plus 0.3 seconds per word of message text.
Write a rule that VoiceOver users get at least 10 seconds before auto-dismiss.
Check that the plan file records both the 6-second base and the 10-second minimum.

K-002145.example: The plan sets a 6-second base, 0.3 seconds per word, and a 10-second VoiceOver minimum. A 12-word message therefore dismisses after 10 seconds under VoiceOver, since 6 plus 3.6 is 9.6 seconds, which is raised to the minimum.
K-002145.check: grep -n seconds docs/toast-accessibility-plan.md prints at least two lines, one containing 6 and one containing 10.
traps: A small model may copy a 3-second iOS default without checking it against the spoken message length.
Write the duration as a stated number, not as long enough.
Do not leave the VoiceOver duration unset.

steps.do: List any existing color sets the project already defines for toasts.
Set the plan minimum for body text to 4.5:1 contrast against the toast background.
Set the plan minimum for the icon and dismiss glyph to 3:1 contrast against the background.
Record the light and dark variants as separate color sets in Assets.xcassets.
Confirm the plan file states both ratios.

K-002146.example: The plan sets text #1C1C1E on background #F2F2F7 in light mode, which clears the 4.5:1 minimum by a wide margin. The close icon must reach 3:1 against the same background, and the dark variant is checked on its own.
K-002146.check: grep -n ':1' docs/toast-accessibility-plan.md prints lines containing 4.5:1 and 3:1.
traps: A small model may check only the text and forget the icon's 3:1 minimum.
Light and dark appearance need separate ratio checks, not one shared value.
Do not claim contrast passes without a stated ratio.

steps.do: Attach an @keydown.esc listener on the menu list element that calls close.
In close, set isOpen to false and then await nextTick before moving focus.
Call focus on the trigger element through its template ref after the menu has closed.
Confirm the escape listener is registered in the file.
Run the Escape focus-return test.

K-002147.example: After the menu opens from a button with id 'actions-btn', pressing Escape hides the list and makes that button the document.activeElement.
K-002147.check: grep prints one line containing keydown.esc, and Playwright prints passed with the activeElement id equal to actions-btn.
traps: Moving focus before the list is hidden can leave focus inside an element that is no longer shown. Await nextTick first.
Adding a key listener to the trigger instead of the menu means Escape does nothing while focus is inside the list.

steps.do: Watch isOpen and, when it becomes true, call focus on the first menu item inside nextTick.
Add tabindex -1 to each menu item so the element can take programmatic focus.
Lint the component to catch unused refs and missing imports.
Run the open focus test.

K-002148.example: Pressing Enter on the trigger with id 'actions-btn' opens the menu, and document.activeElement becomes the element with class 'menu-item' at index 0.
K-002148.check: eslint prints no errors, and Playwright prints 1 passed for the open focus test.
traps: Calling focus before the DOM updates targets a hidden item. Wait for nextTick in the watcher.
Focusing the first item when the menu opens by mouse click can show a focus ring the user did not ask for. Check the open method first.

steps.do: Set min-height and min-width of 44px on each menuitem rule in the style block.
Set the text color and background so the contrast ratio is at least 4.5:1 for normal text.
Confirm the 44px minimum height rule exists in the file.
Run axe against the running menu page.
Confirm axe reports zero color-contrast violations in its output.

K-002149.example: A menuitem with color #1a1a1a on background #ffffff passes the 4.5:1 minimum and has min-height 44px.
K-002149.check: grep prints a line with min-height: 44px, and the axe output reports 0 violations.
traps: Setting 44px only on the text span leaves the clickable area small. Apply the size to the menuitem element itself.
Checking contrast only in the hover state misses the default colors that most users see.

steps.do: Create the component file for the menu.
In script setup, declare a ref named isOpen that starts as false.
Bind aria-expanded on the button to a string made from isOpen so it renders 'true' or 'false'.
Set aria-haspopup to 'menu' and aria-controls to 'actions-menu', the id of the list element.
Confirm the three aria attributes are present in the file.
Confirm the aria-controls value matches the list id actions-menu.
Run the ARIA attribute test, which clicks the button and checks aria-expanded changes from 'false' to 'true'.

K-002150.example: The trigger is a button with id 'actions-btn' and aria-controls 'actions-menu', and isOpen is ref(false). Clicking it sets isOpen to true, so the rendered attribute becomes aria-expanded='true'.
K-002150.check: grep prints three matching lines for aria-haspopup, aria-expanded and aria-controls, and Playwright prints 1 passed with aria-expanded going from 'false' to 'true'.
traps: Binding a raw boolean to aria-expanded without converting it to a string can produce an unexpected value. Use an explicit string.
Forgetting aria-controls leaves screen readers unable to link the button to the list. Give the list an id that matches it.

steps.do: Declare a ref named activeIndex that starts at 0.
Collect item elements with a template ref function that pushes each element into an array ref named itemRefs.
Bind tabindex on each menuitem so the active index gets 0 and every other index gets -1.
Call focus on itemRefs at activeIndex inside nextTick after changing activeIndex.
Confirm the tabindex bindings are present in the component.
Run the roving tabindex unit test.

K-002151.example: With three items and activeIndex set to 1, the second button renders tabindex '0' and the other two render tabindex '-1'.
K-002151.check: grep prints at least one tabindex binding, and Vitest prints 1 passed for the roving tabindex test, which finds exactly one element with tabindex 0.
traps: Using a plain array instead of a reactive array ref means the tabindex update may not re-render. Use ref or reactive for the state.
Setting tabindex 0 on every item puts all of them in the tab order, which defeats the pattern.

steps.do: Give the list element role 'menu' and give each item role 'menuitem'.
Add an @keydown.down listener on the list that calls preventDefault and increases activeIndex by one.
Add an @keydown.up listener on the list that calls preventDefault and decreases activeIndex by one.
Wrap activeIndex with a modulo of the item count so it cycles from the last item back to the first.
Confirm preventDefault appears in both keydown handlers.
Run the keyboard navigation test.

K-002152.example: With four items and activeIndex at 3, pressing ArrowDown sets activeIndex to (3 + 1) % 4, which is 0.
K-002152.check: grep prints at least two preventDefault lines, and Playwright prints 1 passed for the keyboard test, which confirms focus moves from item 4 back to item 1.
traps: Forgetting preventDefault lets the page scroll when the arrow keys are pressed. Call it in each handler.
Without a modulo, activeIndex passes the last item and focus is lost.

steps.do: Create the view file for the toast.
Apply .transition(.move(edge: .top).combined(with: .opacity)) to the toast view inside its parent view.
Wrap the state change that shows the toast in withAnimation(.spring(response: 0.35, dampingFraction: 0.8)).
Confirm the spring response is 0.35 (350ms) in the toast source.
Confirm the top-edge transition is declared once in the toast folder.

K-002153.example: Setting isShowing to true inside withAnimation(.spring(response: 0.35, dampingFraction: 0.8)) slides the toast down from the top edge over about 350ms. Setting it back to false runs the same transition in reverse.
K-002153.check: The rg -n command prints one line containing response: 0.35 (350ms), and the rg -c command prints a count of 1 for ToastView.swift.
traps: Using .animation without a value parameter, which is deprecated and animates unrelated changes.
Forgetting withAnimation, so the transition snaps instead of animating.
Using UIView.animate, which is UIKit rather than SwiftUI.

steps.do: Create the modifier file that holds the toast presentation logic.
Read the setting in the view with @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion).
When the value is true, use a plain .opacity transition with a duration of 0.15 seconds (150ms) and no movement.
Confirm the 0.15 second (150ms) fade duration is in the modifier file.
Confirm the environment value is read in the toast folder.
Confirm the check appears in the modifier file.

K-002154.example: When accessibilityReduceMotion is true, the toast fades in over 0.15s (150ms) instead of sliding in over 0.35s. The grep command should print 1 for ToastModifier.swift.
K-002154.check: The rg -n command on 0.15 prints a line showing the 150ms fade, rg -n prints at least one line that reads accessibilityReduceMotion, and grep -c prints a count of 1 or more for ToastModifier.swift.
traps: Forgetting the environment value, so the slide still plays for users who turned on Reduce Motion.
Removing animation entirely instead of falling back to opacity.
Reading the environment outside the view struct, where the value is not tracked.

steps.do: Create the center file that owns the current toast and its dismiss task.
Store the dismiss work in a Task property and call cancel on it when a new toast replaces the old one.
Inside the task, use try await Task.sleep(for: .seconds(3)) (3000ms) and then set isShowing to false inside withAnimation.
Confirm the 3 second (3000ms) delay is in the toast folder.
Confirm Task.sleep is used in the toast folder.
Confirm no Timer is used anywhere in the toast folder.

K-002155.example: Showing a second toast cancels the 3-second dismiss task for the first, so the new toast stays visible for a full 3 seconds. The grep command prints 0 for every file.
K-002155.check: rg -n -F "seconds(3)" prints one line showing the 3 second delay, rg -n -F prints one line per Task.sleep call, and grep -rc prints :0 for every file in Sources/Toast.
traps: Forgetting to cancel the previous dismiss task, so an old delay hides a new toast early.
Using Timer.scheduledTimer, which is a Foundation pattern and not a SwiftUI idiom.
Hiding the toast without withAnimation, so it disappears with no motion.

steps.do: Store toasts in an array of Identifiable items and render them with ForEach over that array.
Give each toast a UUID id at creation so SwiftUI can track insertions and removals.
Apply .transition(.asymmetric(insertion: .move(edge: .top), removal: .opacity)) to each toast row.
Confirm the asymmetric transition is declared in the toast folder.
Confirm the visible cap constant is set to 3 in the toast folder.
Confirm the insertion slide runs for 0.35 seconds (350ms) in the toast folder.

K-002156.example: Adding a fourth toast when maxVisible is 3 removes the oldest with a fade while the new toast slides in from the top over 350ms. The rg command prints the line containing maxVisible = 3.
K-002156.check: rg -c -F prints 1 or more for the asymmetric transition, rg -n -F prints one line containing maxVisible = 3, and rg -n -F "0.35" prints a line showing the 350ms insertion.
traps: Using an array index as the ForEach id, so removals animate the wrong rows.
Forgetting that the array mutation must run inside withAnimation.
Letting the stack grow past the cap, which pushes toasts off screen.

steps.do: Create the constants file for toast motion values.
Define enum ToastMotion with static let showDuration: Double = 0.35 (350ms) and static let hideDuration: Double = 0.25 (250ms).
Replace each raw duration literal in the other toast files with the matching ToastMotion constant.
Confirm the showDuration constant is set to 0.35 (350ms) in the constants file.
Confirm the literal 0.35 appears only in the constants file.
Count the ToastMotion references in the toast folder.

K-002157.example: ToastView uses ToastMotion.showDuration in place of a raw 0.35, so changing that one constant updates every toast. The rg -l command prints only Sources/Toast/ToastMotion.swift.
K-002157.check: rg -n -F prints one line showing showDuration at 0.35 (350ms), rg -l -F "0.35" prints exactly one path, Sources/Toast/ToastMotion.swift, and rg -c ToastMotion prints a count of 1 or more for each file that uses it.
traps: Leaving a raw 0.35 in one view, so that duration drifts from the others.
Making the constants a var instead of static let, which invites accidental mutation.
Changing a constant's value without re-running the rg check, so an old literal survives.

steps.do: List every Vue file under src.
Count Transition usages in src to see what motion already exists.
Confirm the installed Vue major version is 3.
Create a docs folder for the motion plan.
Create the empty plan file.

K-002158.example: find prints src/components/BaseSelect.vue, rg -c reports 2 matches in that file, and npm ls vue prints vue@3.4.21. The plan file docs/motion/select-plan.md is created to record these findings.
K-002158.check: find lists at least one select .vue file, rg prints a count per file, npm ls vue shows a 3.x.x version, and docs/motion/select-plan.md exists.
traps: Do not assume a Vue 2 API like this.$el; the project uses Vue 3 Composition API. Verify with npm ls vue first.
Do not plan a transition on a component that has no matching .vue file. Run find before writing the plan.

steps.do: Find every existing millisecond duration in src.
Count how many distinct duration values already exist.
Create the docs folder if it is missing.
Write the budget note with the chosen values: enter 150ms, leave 100ms, both under the 200ms limit.

K-002159.example: rg prints src/styles/base.css:12 with 200ms, which sets the ceiling. The plan uses enter 150ms and leave 100ms, both below 200ms.
K-002159.check: rg prints each existing duration with its file and line, and the plan records enter 150ms and leave 100ms, both at or below 200ms.
traps: A small model often picks a duration with no measurement. Always run rg first and cite a real value.
Leave durations are often set shorter than enter durations. Plan both values separately and do not reuse one number for both.

steps.do: Count existing prefers-reduced-motion rules in src.
List Playwright tests that already exist so a reduced-motion test can be added next to them.
Record the plan: wrap the transition CSS in a prefers-reduced-motion: reduce media query that sets the duration to 0ms.

K-002160.example: rg -c prints 0 matches, so no reduced-motion rule exists yet. The plan adds a media query that sets the select transition to 0ms when reduce is set.
K-002160.check: rg prints a count (0 if none exist), npx playwright test --list prints the number of tests found, and the plan names the media query and the 0ms value.
traps: Do not implement the fallback in JavaScript only. Vue's Transition class names need a matching CSS media query to take effect.
Do not skip the test list step. A plan with no test target is not verifiable.

steps.do: Find existing TransitionGroup usages in src.
Count elements with role option in src to size the list.
Check the Vue package version supports TransitionGroup, which is in Vue 3.
Record the plan: use TransitionGroup with tag set to ul and name set to option-fade.

K-002161.example: rg -c role=option reports 12 matches in src/components/BaseSelect.vue. The plan uses TransitionGroup tag ul with name option-fade for those 12 items.
K-002161.check: rg lists TransitionGroup usages or none, rg prints the option count, npm ls vue shows 3.x.x, and the plan names tag ul and name option-fade.
traps: Do not give TransitionGroup items without a stable key. Duplicate or missing keys break leave transitions.
Do not use TransitionGroup for a single element. Use Transition for one element.

steps.do: List the existing Playwright test folder to find where a select test belongs.
Count the Playwright test files that already exist.
Confirm Playwright is installed in the project.
Record the plan: the select must show its panel within 200ms of a click, verified by a test named select-open-timing.

K-002162.example: find tests -name *.spec.ts lists 3 files, and npm ls @playwright/test prints @playwright/test@1.47.0. The plan sets a 200ms open budget and names the test select-open-timing in tests/select.spec.ts.
K-002162.check: ls shows the tests folder, find prints a count of spec files, npm ls shows a version, and the plan states the 200ms budget with the test name.
traps: Do not set a timing target without a test that measures it. A plan with no check cannot be verified later.
Do not use a timing that differs from the 200ms budget set elsewhere in the plan. Keep the number the same everywhere.

steps.do: Choose MAX_VISIBLE as 3 and plan to define it once in the toast store module.
Check that the constant is declared once in the library folder.
Plan the store to hold extra toasts in a queue outside the rendered list.
Confirm the store file compiles and the Svelte checker reports no errors.

K-002163.example: Declare const MAX_VISIBLE = 3 in src/lib/toast.svelte.js and let a fourth toast wait in a queue until one dismisses. The grep should print exactly one declaration line.
K-002163.check: grep prints one line like src/lib/toast.svelte.js:4:const MAX_VISIBLE = 3; and svelte-check ends with 0 errors.
traps: Using slice to drop extra toasts silently loses messages instead of queuing them. Put the limit in the store, not in each host, or two hosts can exceed it.

steps.do: Plan each toast to carry a unique numeric id assigned when it is created.
Check the each block in the host component uses a key expression.
Confirm the key is the id field, not the array index or the message text.
Expect a count of exactly 1 for the keyed each block.

K-002164.example: Write {#each toasts as toast (toast.id)} in src/lib/Toaster.svelte with ids from a counter that increments on each push. The grep should print 1.
K-002164.check: grep -c prints 1, and the rg output shows a single each line containing (toast.id).
traps: Keying by index makes Svelte reuse nodes with the wrong content during dismissals. Keying by message text breaks when two identical toasts appear.

steps.do: Set the budget at under 3 KiB uncompressed for the toast code in the production build.
Build the production bundle so the chunk can be measured.
List built JavaScript files smaller than 3 KiB to confirm the toast chunk fits.
Expect the toast code to appear in a file under 3 KiB, otherwise split or trim it.

K-002165.example: Run npm run build, then find dist -name '*.js' -size -3k should list a file containing the toast component. If the toast code is larger, move the animation helpers out of the component.
K-002165.check: The build exits with status 0 and find prints at least one .js path under dist for the toast chunk.
traps: Measuring the source file instead of the built output gives a false size. Also, find -size rounds in KiB units, so check the number, not just the presence.

steps.do: Install Textual and pytest into the project environment.
Create form.py with a Screen that has Input widgets and a Button with id submit.
In compose, wrap the fields in a Container with id body and yield a LoadingIndicator with id loader.
In the submit handler, set the body container loading flag to True and start the save with self.run_worker.
In the worker's finally block, set the body container loading flag back to False.
Run the test that clicks submit and checks the loading flag during and after the save.

K-002166.example: Clicking Submit sets body.loading to True, and a fake save that sleeps 0.5s keeps it True until the worker finishes. The test asserts loading is True at 0.05s and False at 1.0s.
K-002166.check: pytest prints '1 passed' and both loading assertions pass.
traps: Setting loading on the Button instead of the container leaves the fields editable during the save.
Skipping the finally block leaves the spinner stuck forever when save_form raises.

steps.do: Confirm the installed Textual version supports run_test and Pilot.
Create test_double_submit.py for the double-press test.
In the submit handler, return early if self._busy is already True.
Set the submit Button disabled property to True before starting the worker and back to False in finally.
Run the double submit test.

K-002167.example: The test presses Enter twice within 50ms and a fake save counter ends at 1. The Submit button stays disabled until the worker completes.
K-002167.check: pytest prints '1 passed' and the assertion calls == 1 holds.
traps: Checking only the button state misses a second Enter key path that calls the handler directly.
Skipping the finally block leaves the button disabled after an error.

steps.do: Confirm the installed Textual version provides set_timer on the App and Widget.
Create test_spinner_delay.py for the timing tests.
In the submit handler, call self.set_timer with 0.2 seconds to set body.loading to True, and store the returned Timer.
When the worker completes, call stop on the stored Timer before setting body.loading to False.
Run the timing tests.

K-002168.example: A fake save of 50ms never shows the spinner, while a fake save of 500ms shows it after 0.2s. The test asserts loading is False at 0.1s with the 50ms save.
traps: Passing 200 as milliseconds makes the spinner appear almost instantly, so use 0.2 seconds.
Not stopping the stored Timer lets it fire after the save ended and leaves loading stuck True.

steps.do: Find the cancel method on the Worker class in the installed Textual package.
Store the Worker returned by run_worker in self._save_worker.
Add a BINDINGS entry that maps escape to a cancel_save action, which calls self._save_worker.cancel().
In the worker body, catch asyncio.CancelledError, set body.loading to False, and re-raise it.
Run the cancel test, which presses Escape at 0.1s on a 5s fake save and asserts the run ends within 0.2s.

K-002169.example: A fake save sleeps 5 seconds, and Escape at 0.1s cancels it. The test asserts elapsed < 0.2 and that body.loading is False afterward.
K-002169.check: pytest prints '1 passed' and the elapsed assertion passes.
traps: Swallowing CancelledError without re-raising keeps the worker running after cancel.
Calling cancel on a worker that already finished does nothing, so the loading flag still needs its own reset.

steps.do: Create the Textual stylesheet file for the form.
Create test_layout.py for the layout test.
In form.tcss, give LoadingIndicator with id loader a height of 3 and dock it to the bottom.
Set the App class variable CSS_PATH to form.tcss.
Run the layout test.

K-002170.example: The loader region is 3 rows tall and the body region stays 20 rows both before and during loading. The test compares app.query_one('#body').region.height on each side of the loading toggle.
K-002170.check: pytest prints '1 passed' and both body heights equal 20.
traps: Textual sizes are in cells, so px or rem values are wrong here.
Hiding the loader with display set to False removes it from layout and makes the form jump, so reserve its height instead.

steps.do: Create test_error_clears_loading.py for the error path test.
In the worker, catch exceptions from save_form, set an error Label text, and set body.loading to False in finally.
Make the fake save raise ValueError in the test and assert the error Label is visible.
Run the error path test.

K-002171.example: A fake save raises ValueError after 0.1s, and the test asserts body.loading is False and the error Label text is non-empty. The Submit button is enabled again afterward.
K-002171.check: pytest prints '1 passed' and the loading assertion is False.
traps: Catching the exception without a finally block leaves loading True when the handler returns early.
Showing the error without resetting the Submit button leaves the form stuck until restart.

steps.do: Create the widget file at lib/widgets/responsive_table.dart.
Define const double breakpointCompact = 600 at the top of the file, in logical pixels.
Wrap the table body in LayoutBuilder and branch on constraints.maxWidth against breakpointCompact.
Confirm the breakpoint constant is defined once and compared once, so the count is 2.
Confirm the file imports the Material library.
Confirm the breakpoint value is exactly 600 and note its line number.
Create the widget test file at test/responsive_table_test.dart.
Run make test, the project test target that runs flutter test, including the widget test that pumps the widget at 390 and 720 logical pixels.

K-002172.example: At 720dp the widget returns a DataTable, and at 390dp it returns a ListView.builder of Card rows, both reading the same list of order rows. The breakpoint lives in one constant, so moving it to 840 for an expanded layout changes one line.
K-002172.check: grep -c 'breakpointCompact' prints 2, the grep -n line shows the 600 definition with its line number, grep -c for the material import prints 1, and make test exits with status 0 and reports All tests passed.
traps: Reading MediaQuery width ignores the parent's constraints inside a split pane or drawer.
Writing the 600 literal in two places lets the two branches drift apart.
The 600 breakpoint is in logical pixels, not physical pixels.

steps.do: Set dataRowMinHeight to 48 and headingRowHeight to 56 on the DataTable, in logical pixels.
Read the text scale with MediaQuery.textScalerOf(context).
Clamp the scaler with maxScaleFactor set to 1.3 and apply it to the cell text style.
Confirm the 48 logical pixel row minimum is set once and note its line number.
Count the maxScaleFactor clamp in the widget file, expecting 1.
Create the text scale test file at test/responsive_table_text_scale_test.dart.
Run make test, the project test target that runs flutter test, including a widget test that pumps the table at a text scale of 2.0 and checks each data row is at least 48 logical pixels tall.

K-002173.example: At a system text scale of 2.0, the cell text renders at 1.3 times its base size, and the 48 logical pixel row minimum still fits it. The header row keeps its 56 logical pixel minimum for the same reason.
K-002173.check: The grep -n line shows the dataRowMinHeight: 48 line, grep -c for maxScaleFactor prints 1, and make test exits with status 0 and reports All tests passed, with every data row at least 48 logical pixels tall at text scale 2.0.
traps: Setting a fixed row height below 48 breaks the minimum touch target.
textScaleFactor is deprecated, so use MediaQuery.textScalerOf instead.
Clamping the scale to 1.0 ignores the user's accessibility setting.

steps.do: Confirm the contrast spec file exists in the e2e folder.
Run the spec that sets data-theme to light and then dark, and runs axe on the menu in each.
Count the menu color tokens defined in the token stylesheet.
Check that the spec asserts the color-contrast rule was enabled and not disabled.

K-002174.example: Light text #1a1a1a on #ffffff measures 16.1:1 and dark text #e6e6e6 on #121212 measures 15.1:1, both above the 4.5:1 minimum. The spec fails if axe reports any color-contrast violation on the open menu in either theme.
K-002174.check: Playwright prints '2 passed' and the axe violations array is empty for both light and dark runs. The rg count for menu tokens matches the number of menu color variables in tokens.css.
traps: Testing only the light theme and assuming dark is fine.
Checking contrast with the menu closed, so the open panel and its items are never measured.
Hardcoding hex colors in the Svelte component instead of reading CSS custom properties, which breaks the dark override.

steps.do: Find the line where data-theme is set in the app shell HTML template.
Find the line where the SvelteKit body placeholder is inserted.
Run the no-flash spec that reloads the page with a stored dark preference and records the first painted theme.
Confirm the theme init script is inline and not imported as a module.

K-002175.example: If data-theme is set on line 3 of app.html and sveltekit.body is on line 12, the script runs before body content renders. The no-flash spec records the first computed background color as the dark value.
K-002175.check: The data-theme line number is smaller than the sveltekit.body line number, and the Playwright spec prints '1 passed'. The module count rg returns 0 because the script is inline.
traps: Putting the theme script in a Svelte component, which runs after hydration and causes a flash.
Adding type=module to the init script, which defers it and reintroduces the flash.
Reading localStorage without a try and catch, so a blocked storage error stops the init script.

steps.do: Confirm the system theme spec file exists.
Run the spec that emulates dark color scheme and checks the data-theme attribute on the html element.
Confirm the component listens for matchMedia changes on the dark query.

K-002176.example: The spec calls emulateMedia with colorScheme dark, then expects the html data-theme attribute to equal dark within 200ms. A second case switches to light and expects light within the same window.
K-002176.check: Playwright prints '2 passed' and the rg output shows one matchMedia call with prefers-color-scheme dark.
traps: Reading matchMedia once at module load and never subscribing to changes.
Setting the attribute only on the menu element instead of the html root, so other components keep the wrong theme.
Forgetting to remove the change listener when the component unmounts.

steps.do: Run the persistence spec that toggles the menu theme, reloads the page, and checks the selected option.
Count the localStorage reads and writes in the theme store module.
Run the store unit tests for the Svelte rune state.

K-002177.example: The user selects dark, the store writes theme=dark to localStorage, and after reload the menu radio for dark is checked. The spec times this round trip under 200ms.
K-002177.check: Playwright prints '1 passed'. The rg output shows one getItem and one setItem call. Vitest prints 'Tests 3 passed'.
traps: Storing the theme in $state only, which resets on reload.
Writing localStorage on every render inside $effect, causing extra writes and loops.
Not handling the system option, so storage keeps a stale explicit value.

steps.do: Run the focus spec that tabs through menu items in dark mode and reads the computed outline.
Confirm the focus-visible selector is used for menu items.
Confirm the focus ring token is defined for dark mode.

K-002178.example: The spec tabs to the third menu item and reads outline width 2px and outline color #8ab4f8 against the #121212 background, a contrast of 7.2:1. The minimum target height is checked as 44px.
K-002178.check: Playwright prints '1 passed'. The focus-visible count is at least 1, and the rg output shows a focus-ring token inside the dark theme block.
traps: Using outline none on menu items and relying only on background color for focus.
Using a focus color that matches the dark background, which gives roughly 1:1 contrast.
Checking focus only on the first item and missing the rest of the list.
